To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the tolerogenic potential of semi-mature BM-DC to induce protective type II NKT and CD4+ T helper cell responses is enhanced in the absence of the co-inhibition molecule B7-H2.
B7-H1 deficiency enhances the tolerogenic capacity of semi-mature BM-derived DC by activating type II NKT cell responses.
B7-H1 is a negative regulator of type II NKT cell responses, which are essential for the tolerogenic potential of BM-DC.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel immunotherapeutic approaches for autoimmune diseases.
the role of DC as tolerogenic APC and with the mechanisms by which B7-H1 regulates the function of NKT cells in the context of autoimmune diseases.
the development and application of a novel tolerogenic DC therapy in EAE.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the B7-H1 molecule on DC is not required to generate tolerogenic responses but it does inhibit type II NKT cell activation and thereby enhances the tolerogenic potential of DC.
the absence of B6-H1 on DC results in a stronger activation of type II NKT cell responses which in turn results in an increase of tolerogenic responses.
in absence of B7H1, the tolerogenic potential of BM-derived DC is enhanced.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
B7-H1 deficiency on DC enhances tolerogenicity by activation of type II NKT cell.
B7-H1 inhibits type II NKT cell activation and that B7-H2 (PD-L2, CD273) is not expressed by BM-DC.
B7-H1 is a negative regulator of type II NKT cell activation by semi-mature BM-derived DC.
The main takeaway from our work is that
B7-H1 can inhibit NKT cell activation in the absence of T cell receptor engagement and can be exploited to enhance NKT cell responses in the context of autoimmunity.
B7-H1 can be a target in DC therapy for autoimmune diseases.
B7-H1 is a key negative regulator of NKT cells.
